Parse banded category labels into numeric bounds

Source: R/bands.R
prsbands.Rd

Published administrative tables often report intervals instead of values: “18 to 24”, “2 to 5”, "50+", “Greater than 15 days”. This function reads such labels into a lower and an upper bound per band, and flags the bands that are open at the top or the bottom. It recognises the wordings open-data publishers actually use, and leaves a label it cannot read as NA rather than guessing. Use it as the first step before bandvals, expbands or bandsens.

Usage

prsbands(x, clsup = TRUE, intsca = TRUE)

Arguments

x

Character vector (or factor) of band labels.

clsup

Logical, default TRUE. For the inclusive open-upper wordings ("+", "and over", "or more" and the like), whether the stated number belongs to the band: TRUE reads "50+" as 50 and above, FALSE as above 50 (lower bound 51 on an integer scale). The exclusive wordings ("greater than 15") always exclude the number.

intsca

Logical, default TRUE. Whether the quantity is integer-valued (counts, days, whole years). It decides whether "greater than 15" starts at 16 (TRUE) or at 15 as an infimum (FALSE). A label written with decimals is always treated as continuous.

Value

A data frame with one row per label and columns label (character, as given), lower and upper (numeric bounds, NA for the open side of an open band or for an unparsed label), and openlo, openup (logical).

Details

Labels are lower-cased and trimmed; the Unicode dash family (U+2010 to U+2015 and the minus sign U+2212) is read as a hyphen, and correctly grouped thousands separators are removed ("1,000 to 2,499"). Then, in order:

  • Closed range: two numbers joined by to, - or through, optionally preceded by one word and followed by a unit ("ages 18-24", "0 to 5 overnight stays"). The two numbers must be the only numbers in the label, the lower must not exceed the upper, and no open-band cue word (over, under, more, less, plus, ...) or + may appear; otherwise the label is NA.

  • Open upper band, inclusive: "50+", "65 and over", "and above", "or more", "or over", "plus". The lower bound is the number when clsup = TRUE, and the number plus one step otherwise.

  • Open upper band, exclusive: "greater than", "more than", "over", "above", "gt". The lower bound is the number plus one step.

  • Open lower band, inclusive: "17 and under", "or less", "or fewer", "and below", "or under". The upper bound is the number.

  • Open lower band, exclusive: "less than", "fewer than", "under", "below", "<", "lt". The upper bound is the number minus one step.

  • Bare number: a band of width zero. A bare negative number ("-5") is read as a suppressed cell and stays NA.

The step is 1 when intsca = TRUE and the label has no decimal point, and 0 otherwise. A label with more than one number that is not a range, an empty label and NA all give NA bounds. Anything other than a character or factor vector is an error.

References

The forms recognised here are taken from the categories the Ontario Ministry of the Solicitor General publishes in its inmate datasets (the segregation and restrictive-confinement releases), where the placement-count and age categories are banded and the top band is open.

See also

bandvals, bandsens, expbands

Examples

prsbands(c("1", "2 to 5", "6 to 10", "Greater than 10"))
#>             label lower upper openlo openup
#> 1               1     1     1  FALSE  FALSE
#> 2          2 to 5     2     5  FALSE  FALSE
#> 3         6 to 10     6    10  FALSE  FALSE
#> 4 Greater than 10    11    NA  FALSE   TRUE

prsbands(c("18 to 24", "25 to 49", "50+", "under 18"))
#>      label lower upper openlo openup
#> 1 18 to 24    18    24  FALSE  FALSE
#> 2 25 to 49    25    49  FALSE  FALSE
#> 3      50+    50    NA  FALSE   TRUE
#> 4 under 18    NA    17   TRUE  FALSE

# "50+" excluding 50, and a continuous scale
prsbands(c("50+", "over 15"), clsup = FALSE)
#>     label lower upper openlo openup
#> 1     50+    51    NA  FALSE   TRUE
#> 2 over 15    16    NA  FALSE   TRUE
prsbands(c("over 15", "under 0.5"), intsca = FALSE)
#>       label lower upper openlo openup
#> 1   over 15    15    NA  FALSE   TRUE
#> 2 under 0.5    NA   0.5   TRUE  FALSE

# An unrecognised or self-contradictory label is NA, not guessed at.
prsbands(c("3", "unknown", "24 to 18", "15 to 19 and over"))
#>               label lower upper openlo openup
#> 1                 3     3     3  FALSE  FALSE
#> 2           unknown    NA    NA  FALSE  FALSE
#> 3          24 to 18    NA    NA  FALSE  FALSE
#> 4 15 to 19 and over    NA    NA  FALSE  FALSE

try(prsbands(1:3))
#> Error : `x` must be character band labels
